visual.title: Ascitic neutrophil count
visual.label: 400 cells/µl
visual.caption: Over 250 neutrophils/µl on paracentesis confirms SBP; E. coli is the commonest organism.
Free air under the diaphragm when perforation is suspected.

visuals.title: SBP without a hole
visuals.text: Cirrhosis causes ascites; bacteria reach it by translocation across the gut wall or through the blood.

glossary.peritoneal lining: The thin membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering the organs.
glossary.intra-abdominal infection: Infection inside the abdominal cavity, such as an abscess or appendicitis.
glossary.perforated duodenal ulcer: An ulcer in the first part of the small bowel that has burst through the wall.
glossary.bowel obstruction: A blockage stopping bowel contents passing along.
glossary.bowel ischaemia: Lack of blood supply to the bowel.
glossary.inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as WCC and CRP that rise with inflammation.
glossary.tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.instrumentation: Passing instruments into the body, such as an endoscope, which can perforate the bowel.
glossary.luminal: On the inside of the hollow bowel.
glossary.spontaneous bacterial peritonitis: Infection of ascitic fluid with no perforation or surgical cause, seen in cirrhosis.
glossary.neutrophil: The commonest white blood cell, which fights bacterial infection.
glossary.cells/µl: Cells per microlitre, the unit for counting cells in a fluid sample.
glossary.ascitic fluid culture: Growing the ascitic fluid in the lab to identify the bacteria.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.gold standard: The best available test for confirming the diagnosis.
glossary.free air under diaphragm: Gas escaped from the bowel collecting under the diaphragm on an upright film.
glossary.broad-spectrum IV antibiotics: Antibiotics covering many bacteria, given through a vein.
glossary.drainage: Letting out pus or fluid, often with a tube.
glossary.prophylaxis: Treatment given to prevent a problem coming back.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction from the body's response to infection.
glossary.urine output: How much urine is passed; falls as the kidneys are poorly perfused.
glossary.resuscitation: Urgent treatment to restore breathing, circulation and blood pressure.
glossary.hollow viscus: A hollow organ such as the stomach or bowel.
glossary.chemical irritation: Inflammation caused by acid or bile rather than bacteria.
glossary.bacterial contamination: Bacteria entering a normally sterile space.
glossary.localised peritonitis: Peritoneal inflammation limited to one area, such as around the appendix.
glossary.generalised peritonitis: Inflammation spread across the whole peritoneum.
glossary.systemic inflammatory response: Body-wide inflammation with fever, fast heart rate and leaky vessels.
glossary.reflex contraction: Automatic tightening of a muscle without conscious control.
glossary.haematogenous spread: Spread of infection through the bloodstream.
glossary.gut wall: The layers of the bowel wall between the lumen and the peritoneal cavity.
